title: Design System: Ben Kaufman — Executive Producer

display.purpose: The hero name on the home reel. Once per site, 8vw, bottom-left inside the framelines.

headline.purpose: The About name, mobile menu items, full-screen overlay titles.

title.purpose: Names of works — project titles on hover, photograph captions. Always italic.

body.purpose: Prose. The bio paragraph is the only body copy on the site; capped at 480px, 75% opacity.

label.purpose: Navigation links and the skip link. Helvetica 11px at 0.25em, uppercase.

caption.purpose: The smallest functional voice: EXECUTIVE PRODUCER, client names, eyebrows, footnotes. 9px at 0.3–0.4em.

data.purpose: Machine readings — timecode, HUD telemetry, lightbox counters, Vimeo credit blocks. Never prose or navigation.

motion.name: cut
motion.purpose: Page-to-page cross-fade and the false-colour filter swap. The fastest move in the system.

motion.name: quick
motion.purpose: Lightbox backdrop fade, colour and opacity changes on controls, cursor state changes.

motion.name: standard
motion.purpose: Thumbnail scale to 1.03, scrim fade-in, hamburger fold, contact-link opacity.

motion.name: considered
motion.purpose: Nav opacity 0.5 → 1.0, mobile menu cross-fade, IRIS clip-path change, click ripple, tile entrance.

motion.name: held
motion.purpose: HUD fade-up, About column entrance, overlay title reveals.

motion.name: cinematic
motion.purpose: The home reel resolving out of black. The longest transition permitted.

motion.name: stagger
motion.purpose: Delay between grid items on entrance. Photography cycles the multiplier every 12 items.

motion.name: ease-default
motion.purpose: The only CSS easing used. No cubic-bezier overshoot, no spring, no bounce.

narrative.overview:
Everything in this system behaves like the feed on a director's monitor. The picture runs full-bleed and uninterrupted; the interface lives in the margins as instrumentation — framelines at 10vh, a live 24fps timecode, FPS / SHUTTER / IRIS / EI / ND / WB readouts, a STBY indicator that flips to REC after ten seconds. None of it decorates the image. It surrounds it, the way a monitor's overlay surrounds a take, and it implies a person who reads those numbers for a living.

The register is precise, nocturnal and unshowy. Technical exactness in near-darkness: a #0C0C0C void that is deliberately not black, warm parchment text that is deliberately not white, one gold that never fills anything, and a serif that appears only for names and titles. Confidence is expressed as restraint — no element raises its voice, and nothing is explained. The audience is film people; the system speaks their language without translating it.

The site is emphatically not a creative-agency template, a SaaS product page, a stock photographer's portfolio theme, or a show-reel gimmick site. Those four are binding anti-references. The distinction from the last one is the sharpest and the easiest to lose: every effect here is diegetic — it exists because a camera, a projector or a lens does that. A projector hum plays as a film loads because projectors hum. Grain sits at 8% over every page because film has grain. The moment an effect stops being something a piece of film equipment actually does, it becomes the gimmick site.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black void (#0C0C0C), warm parchment text (#E8E4DC), one dark gold accent used at hairline scale
Cormorant Garamond 300 for names and titles only; Helvetica Neue for UI; DM Sans for prose; JetBrains Mono for machine data
Zero corner radius everywhere except literal optics (rings, dots, the countdown circle)
No shadows in the entire system — depth is scrim, grain, vignette and defocus
Edge-to-edge grids separated by a single 1px hairline, never gutters or cards
Slow motion: 200–1400ms, ease and easeOut, no springs, no bounce
A custom cursor replaces the system cursor globally (cursor: none !important)

rules.name: The Tungsten Rule
rules.body: Tungsten Gold is applied at hairline scale only: a 1px rule, a 9px label, a focus ring, one active word. If it covers more than a line or a word, it's wrong. Its rarity is what makes it read as gold rather than as a brand colour.

rules.name: The No-Pure Rule
rules.body: No surface is #000000 and no text is #FFFFFF. The only exceptions are diegetic: the film leader's flash frame, the projector gate flash, and the HUD's white readouts, all of which are accurate to the equipment they imitate.

rules.name: The Instrument Quarantine Rule
rules.body: HUD Amber, REC Red and STBY Green belong to the camera overlay. They never appear as UI feedback, never as a link colour, never as a state on a button.

rules.name: The Serif-Speaks-Once Rule
rules.body: Cormorant is for proper nouns — the name, and the title of a work. It never runs a sentence, never labels a control, never appears below 13px.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for readings a machine would produce: timecode, frame IDs, counters, credit blocks pulled from Vimeo. Never prose, never navigation, never a heading.

rules.name: The Wide-Small Rule
rules.body: Functional type gets smaller and wider together. At 9px the tracking is 0.3–0.4em; at 11px it is 0.25em. Small type is never set tight — the space is what makes it legible against a moving image.

rules.name: The No-Gutter Rule
rules.body: Work images butt against each other. The only separation permitted between two pieces of work is a 1px hairline. No cards, no padding, no drop-shadowed tiles.

rules.name: The Frameline Rule
rules.body: On the home reel, nothing of consequence lives outside the 10vh framelines. The HUD reads in the margins above and below; the name reads inside the frame.

rules.name: The Optical Depth Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, ever. If something needs to separate from what's behind it, it gets a scrim, a blur or a vignette — never a lift.

rules.name: The Stacking Order
rules.body: Reading upward from the picture: video (1) → bottom scrim (3) → false colour (4) → top scrim (8) → framelines (90) → HUD (100) → header (100) → lightboxes (200–500) → idle and easter-egg overlays (9500–10000) → grain (9999) → cursor (99999). Grain sits above everything except the cursor, so nothing in the interface is ever cleaner than the image.

rules.name: The Zero Radius Rule
rules.body: Nothing rectangular is ever rounded. A rounded corner anywhere in this system is a bug, not a preference.

dos: Do keep Tungsten Gold (#8B6914) at hairline scale — a 1px rule, a 9px label, a focus ring, one active word. Never a fill.
Do butt work images edge to edge, separated by nothing thicker than a 1px #2a2a2a seam.
Do build depth from scrims, 8% grain, vignettes and backdrop blur. Never a shadow.
Do set every corner to 0 radius; reserve circles for optics and signals.
Do reserve Cormorant Garamond for proper nouns, and JetBrains Mono for readings a machine would produce.
Do keep transitions between 200ms and 1400ms on ease / easeOut, and stagger grid entrances at 40ms.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion by skipping the projector warm-up, the scale transitions and the staggers — every component already branches on useReducedMotion().
Do carry data-cursor on any new interactive surface so the custom cursor knows what it is over.
Do measure the real header height at runtime when padding a page beneath it.
Do keep new effects diegetic: if a camera, a projector or a lens doesn't do it, it doesn't belong.
donts: Don't introduce box-shadow, border-radius, pure #000 surfaces or pure #FFF text.
Don't use HUD Amber, REC Red or STBY Green as interface colours — they are quarantined to the camera overlay.
Don't extend the full HUD, framelines or timecode beyond the home reel. Mono machine-data type is available everywhere; the instrument layer is not.
Don't underline a link or animate an underline in any state. Opacity 0.5 → 1.0 over 600ms is the entire hover language for text.
Don't add gutters, cards, containers or a max-width column to a work grid.
Don't set functional type tight — at 9–11px the tracking is 0.25em or wider.
Don't restore the system cursor with cursor: pointer on new elements; the global rule is cursor: none.
Don't add spring physics, bounce easing, parallax or scroll-jacking. Slow cinema, not app UI.
Don't put a page title above a grid. The work identifies itself; the h1 stays screen-reader-only.
Don't let it drift toward an agency template, a SaaS product page, a stock-photography portfolio theme, or an effects-for-their-own-sake reel site.
